investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable by the Kubernetes scheduler: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state, so the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create was entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for new peer-pod VMs. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found for incoming pod"). Because the pod never scheduled, the runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (lines 1880–1885) could not reach the createAgent call, and no evidence was written, causing a total contract gap (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote agent VMs are consuming all available peer-pod slots, leaving zero capacity for new probe pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the schedulable pool to those 2 already-exhausted nodes. This is structural and would persist even if some VMs were freed on the wrong nodes.

[Possible] Peer-pod VM slots not being released after previous eval runs: if prior probe agents were not cleaned up (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1883 may not have completed), leaked VMs could be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations.

[Possible] Cluster autoscaler not adding kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes: if autoscaling is configured, it may not be provisioning additional peer-pod-capable nodes fast enough or at all, leaving the pool statically constrained at 2 nodes.

[Low likelihood] Transient scheduler state: a brief spike in concurrent remote agent creation by other workloads could have temporarily exhausted capacity; however, the identical failure across all three sequential sibling checks spanning ~7 minutes (19:37–19:44 UTC) argues against a transient blip.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes have zero available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (2 nodes show Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 nodes did not match pod affinity/selector), preventing any remote agent pod from being scheduled. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs could not reach createAgent() and therefore produced zero evidence, causing the remote-agent-state contract (requiring orgId, agentId, readyState, state) to be entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm peer-pod VM resource quota across all eligible nodes. Of the 6 nodes in the cluster, only 2 support the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity; the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. As a result, every remote agent pod submitted by the eval runner is stuck Unschedulable, the agent is never created, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is ever written — causing the remote-agent-state eval to fail its expected-output contract. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable by the Kubernetes scheduler: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state, so the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for new peer-pod VMs. Preemption was also ruled out ("No preemption victims found for incoming pod"). Because the pod never scheduled, the runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (lines 1880–1885) could not reach the createAgent call, and no evidence was written, causing a total contract gap (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote agent VMs are consuming all available peer-pod slots, leaving zero capacity for new probe pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

[Likely contributing] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, reducing the schedulable pool to those 2 already-exhausted nodes. This is structural and would persist even if some VMs were freed on the wrong nodes.

[Possible] Peer-pod VM slots not being released after previous eval runs: if prior probe agents were not cleaned up (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1883 may not have completed), leaked VMs could be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations.

[Possible] Cluster autoscaler not adding kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes: if autoscaling is configured, it may not be provisioning additional peer-pod-capable nodes fast enough or at all, leaving the pool statically constrained at 2 nodes.

[Low likelihood] Transient scheduler state: a brief spike in concurrent remote agent creation by other workloads could have temporarily exhausted capacity; however, the identical failure across all three sequential sibling checks spanning ~7 minutes (19:37–19:44 UTC) argues against a transient blip.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Exhaustion: kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Depleted Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes swarm cluster was reported Unschedulable: 2 nodes had Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, so pods remained stuck unscheduled for 129–147 seconds before the evals timed out and returned empty evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class, and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod could be scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1918) never completed, the agent lifecycle never advanced, and the eval returned zero evidence — violating all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) defined in check-expectations.json lines 266–269. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes satisfy, so the cluster has no fallback scheduling target even if VM slots were freed.

Tertiary — a concurrent workload spike or leaked/zombie remote-agent pods from a prior eval run may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, preventing new allocations. The eval runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) but a prior failed cleanup could leave orphaned pods consuming capacity.

Lower confidence — a cluster-level configuration change (node count reduction, resource quota tightening, or node affinity rule change) may have reduced the effective VM pool size, but no such change appears in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges.
